steps.title: Look at the two questions.
steps.prompt: When do we use how many?
steps.why: how many + countable, how much + uncountable.
steps.html:
How much rice do you eat?

How many lemons do you need?

steps.title: Quantifiers
steps.html:
CountableUncountable
QuestionHow many lemons?How much rice?
A big amounta lot of / many lemonsa lot of / much rice
A small amounta few lemonsa little rice
Less than you neednot enough lemonsnot enough rice
More than you needtoo many lemonstoo much rice

a lot of works with both, so it is the safe choice in a positive sentence.

much and many are most natural in negatives and questions: We don't have much time.

too means it is a problem: too much salt is not a good thing.

steps.title: Saying numbers
steps.html:
TypeHow to say it
Fractions¼ a quarter · ⅓ a third · ½ a half · ¾ three-quarters
Percentages15% fifteen per cent · 4.7% four point seven per cent
Decimals2.89 two point eight nine · 0.3 nought point three
Temperatures22°C twenty-two degrees Celsius · −7°C minus seven
Big numbers3,000,000 three million

After the decimal point, say each figure separately: 2.89 is two point eight nine.

million has no -s after a number: three million people.

steps.title: Plov for six people
steps.html:
Ingredients: half a kilo of beef, a kilo of rice, four carrots, two onions, a little oil and some salt.

Chop the onions and the carrots. Heat the oil and fry the beef. Add the vegetables and a little salt. Then add the rice and some water. Don't add too much water, and don't add it quickly – add a little at a time. Cook for forty minutes. Add a few raisins at the end, mix, and serve!

steps.title: How much food do countries grow?
steps.html: Papua New Guinea grows about three-quarters of its food. Singapore is very different: it grows less than 10 per cent. There isn't enough land in a city-state, so it imports a lot of food. Indonesia grows a lot of rice, and forty million people work on farms – one sixth of all Indonesians. But Indonesians eat a lot of rice, and the country still imports about three million tonnes a year.
